If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The failing test `testMySqlNullOutput` uses a CSVFormat configured for MySQL output with a null string "NULL" and quoting enabled with quote mode NON_NUMERIC. The expected output is that the string "NULL" is quoted, but the actual null value (null) is output as NULL without quotes. The test expects the output line to be "\"NULL\"\tNULL\n".

Inspecting the CSVPrinter.printRecord(Object...) method shows that it calls print(Object) for each value. The print(Object) method turns the null value into the nullString via `format.getNullString()` if the value is null, then calls print(Object, CharSequence, int, int) with that nullString's characters.

In print(Object, CharSequence, int, int), the logic first appends delimiters if needed, then checks if the format has a quote character set. If so, it calls printAndQuote, else if the format has an escape character, it calls printAndEscape, else it writes the characters directly.

The issue raised in the bug report is that `printAndEscape` will escape characters in the nullString, which is undesirable for generating MySQL dumps, as the null string representation (such as \N) should be output literally. The test wants the null string "NULL" to be output without escaping, but quotes applied if needed.

Currently, if the CSVFormat is set with an escape character, and the null string contains characters that are matched by printAndEscape, they get escaped incorrectly (e.g., "\\N" turning into "\"\\N\"").

Hence, the root cause is that printAndEscape applies escaping to the null string representation, which should not be escaped. The code does not differentiate the null string from regular strings for escaping, leading to incorrect output.

The desired fix is to modify CSVPrinter to avoid escaping the null string when printing it, and instead print it as is, possibly quoted, to fit MySQL null literal expectations.

The recent bug report is not very relevant here; it concerns comment line processing, unrelated to null string escaping.

Summary: The escaping logic in printAndEscape should be skipped or modified when printing the null string (obtained from CSVFormat.getNullString) so that it outputs the null string literally without adding escape characters.

The issue manifests in print(Object) which converts null values to the nullString, followed by print(...) which currently calls printAndEscape for escaping that string erroneously.

Fixes should focus on CSVPrinter.print(...) and/or CSVPrinter.printAndEscape(...) to change behavior regarding the nullString escaping.

This matches the current bug summary and test failure perfectly.
org.apache.commons.csv.CSVPrinter.print(java.lang.Object, java.lang.CharSequence, int, int)
org.apache.commons.csv.CSVPrinter.printAndEscape(java.lang.CharSequence, int, int)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
